A seeded event's id is `_ulidFor(key, ts)` -- eighty bits of randomness from the key and forty-eight of time from the timestamp -- and the randomness is identical on the two rigs while the time is not: the note at index 5199 is `01KPV0SDX06FA58CJ9JXH23W7R` under `flutter test` and `0002V0SDX06FA58CJ9JXH23W7R` in the captured PWA, same twenty-two-character tail, different four-character head. So an id read off the test rig names nothing in the capture, `indexWhere` returns -1, `_scrollToAnchor` returns without scrolling, and the shot is taken wherever the thread was standing -- which is the end of it, and six notes. That is exactly what happened in this firing's first capture. An INDEX is the same on both rigs: both read 8387 items, and 0.622 is item 5216 in each. Why 5216: 0.62 landed on a run of long notes and put seven notes on the screen against an exit condition of eight, and firing 21's 40-logical search margin was blamed for the eighth. Measured at firing 37, that is not what took it -- at that anchor the region can be given 40, 60 or 100 more logical pixels and the visible span does not move at all, because the next note costs between 65 and 104. So the shot is framed rather than the screen re-cut. 5216 is the densest stretch in a sweep of the thread either side of the old anchor: twelve notes in frame on the test rig with twelve distinct tears and no repeat, against nine there for the old anchor and seven in the capture.
